label: rem:stable-atom-properties
title: Properties of ILP stability
html:
Independence of neighborhood. Stability is a fixed-q property. It does not require the ILP to be feasible on a neighborhood of q. An atom may be stable at q_0 and unstable at q_0 + \epsilon without contradiction. Stability tracks ILP-feasibility pointwise.

Connection to LP-feasibility. The continuous LP relaxation (x \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^N, \mathrm{G}(q) x \geq 0) is always feasible, since the trivial identity normal form T_e = e_{(k)} has y_{(k)} = 0. The ILP version is strictly stronger.

Confined operators only. One solves the ILP within the confinement filtration (confinement level) at q. One only considers primitives e_\lambda in J^{\ell(K, q)}(q), since operators above the atom's confinement level are unavailable without further phase transitions.

Scope of the stability condition. For a stable atom, the Frobenius positivity constraint (\mathrm{G}x)_\gamma \geq 0 holds for every primitive constraint \gamma at the coefficient vector of T_w itself. The condition is evaluated at the vector x(K, q) fixed by the decomposition of T_w, not at an arbitrary vector. The existential form \exists\, x \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^N with \mathrm{G}(q)\,x \geq 0 holds for every atom, since x = 0 satisfies it, and therefore does not distinguish stable from unstable atoms.
